claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18, his eligibility depends on whether he's still in approved education or training. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 if they meet certain conditions.

Could you tell me, is Alex currently in any of the following:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)
- An approved training course (not paid for by an employer)

Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex has left education. He's not studying at the moment - he finished school and isn't doing any courses or training right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

I have one more question to confirm: Does Alex live with you, and are you responsible for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the official Child Benefit eligibility rules, I now have enough information to make a decision about Alex's eligibility.

Unfortunately, since Alex is 18 years old and has left education (he's not in approved education or training), he no longer qualifies for Child Benefit.

The rules state that:
- You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child **under 16**
- If your child is 16 or over, you'll only continue to qualify if they stay in **approved education or training** until they're under 20

There is one potential exception: If Alex has recently left education (within the last 20 weeks) and he's registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you may be able to apply for Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks. However, this only applies to 16 or 17 year olds, not 18 year olds.

Let me record this outcome for you:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary of Eligibility Decision**

I'm sorry to say that you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:** Alex is 18 years old and has left education. Child Benefit for children aged 16 and over only continues if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is not currently studying or in approved training, he no longer meets the eligibility requirements.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he enrols in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels or certain vocational qualifications) before turning 20 - you may become eligible again at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
